Remap table for overlaying LCC 2020 onto the simulation land cover

Source: R/current-conditions.R
lcc2020_remap_table.Rd

Builds the remapTable that LandR::overlayLCCs() uses to decide, for every combination of a simulation land-cover code (LCC, SCANFI-derived) and a current-condition LCC 2020 code (CC), which code the pixel ends up with. Promoted verbatim from LandWeb_preamble, which mirrors LandWeb v2's rule ordering with LCC 2020 codes substituted for v2's CC 0-5.

lcc2020_remap_table(
  lccClasses,
  ccClasses,
  treeClassesToReplace,
  classes = lcc2020_classes()
)

Arguments

lccClasses

integer vector of the simulation land-cover codes present (NA is added).

ccClasses

integer vector of the LCC 2020 codes present; NAs are dropped, then NA is added back as its own row.

treeClassesToReplace

integer vector of LCC codes that must be reclassified (set to 99).

classes

class groups, as returned by lcc2020_classes().

Value

A data.table with integer columns LCC, CC and newLCC, one row per combination.

Details

Rule order matters: later rules overwrite earlier ones. In order:

  1. LCC 0, 20, 30 -> NA;

  2. CC missing or cropland -> keep LCC;

  3. CC non-flammable (barren/water/snow-ice) -> NA;

  4. CC forest, shrub/grass/moss or wetland -> keep LCC;

  5. LCC missing but CC forest -> 99;

  6. CC urban -> 99;

  7. LCC in treeClassesToReplace -> 99.

CC does not override the simulation's forest determination: every CC class except barren/water/snow-ice defers to LCC, so LCC 2020 calling a treed wetland "wetland" does not strip forest from the simulation.

Note that rule 1 is overwritten by rules 2-6 for every code in the LCC 2020 legend, so it only takes effect for a CC value outside that legend. It is kept for fidelity with v2 rather than removed, and the behaviour is pinned by a test.

Examples

lcc2020_remap_table(
  lccClasses = c(20L, 30L, 210L, 220L),
  ccClasses = c(1L, 14L, 17L, 18L),
  treeClassesToReplace = 240L
)
#> Indices: <LCC>, <CC>
#>       LCC    CC newLCC
#>     <int> <int>  <int>
#>  1:    NA    NA     NA
#>  2:    20    NA     20
#>  3:    30    NA     30
#>  4:   210    NA    210
#>  5:   220    NA    220
#>  6:    NA     1     99
#>  7:    20     1     20
#>  8:    30     1     30
#>  9:   210     1    210
#> 10:   220     1    220
#> 11:    NA    14     NA
#> 12:    20    14     20
#> 13:    30    14     30
#> 14:   210    14    210
#> 15:   220    14    220
#> 16:    NA    17     99
#> 17:    20    17     99
#> 18:    30    17     99
#> 19:   210    17     99
#> 20:   220    17     99
#> 21:    NA    18     NA
#> 22:    20    18     NA
#> 23:    30    18     NA
#> 24:   210    18     NA
#> 25:   220    18     NA
#>       LCC    CC newLCC
#>     <int> <int>  <int>
